campaigns/dungeonvice.title: DungeonVice (2025)
campaigns/dungeonvice.content:
DungeonVice (2025)
A 2025 campaign DM’d by Jake, following a team of city inspectors — part detective squad, part
magic-powered task force — working cases for the Council of Turgeth. Only session 3 has been
transcribed and extracted so far; sessions 1 and 2 are not yet in the archive, so the party’s formation
and earlier cases are unknown. As of session 3 the campaign is mid-arc, hunting a new troll crime lord
and dangling a lead on a devil-bargain and a city-wide drug conspiracy.
The party

Rich (played by Rich) — Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice), a monk (Crane Style, Stunning Strike, flurry of
blows); carries the party’s shared platinum piece in his handy haversack.
Nutty (played by Nutty) — Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice), an arcane combatant wielding a
bladed tail weapon, casting Web and a touch-spell/weapon combo nicknamed “Washashaka.”
Ozan (played by Ozan) — Ozone, a bard-type with a disguise kit/hat of disguise, a net as signature
weapon, and Glitter Dust.
Pat (played by Pat) — Pat’s Wizard (DungeonVice), a wizard, mostly absent in session 3.

Not present in session 3: Donnie, Jess, Connor — unknown whether they have characters in this campaign.
Timeline

Sessions 1–2 — not yet recorded/transcribed.
2025-03-31 — The inspectors interrogate a prisoner who engineered her
own capture to hunt a golden ticket to hell, learn the drug Maka is secretly run by the
College of Turgeth, and raid a dockside warehouse belonging to The Boot, killing Fugly
(nicknamed “the captain” by the players mid-fight — see The Guard Captain) before the Boot escapes
by ship — session ends mid-chase.

Major threads
Resolved

The warehouse raid itself — guards killed, Fugly dead, the warehouse burned
2025-03-31

Dangling / open

Hunt for the Boot — the Boot himself escaped by ship, last seen with Rich in pursuit, hasted and
ethereal, as the ship left harbor.
Golden Ticket to the Devil — the prisoner’s one-way pass to the devil holding her husband
Riggs’s soul was never retrieved.
College of Turgeth Drug Pipeline — the college is secretly the source of the drug Maka, worth
~75,000 gp/week; not yet investigated directly.
Aqueducts Assignment — offered by Volto at the top of the session, not pursued.

Unresolved
Sessions 1 and 2 of this campaign have not yet been transcribed/extracted, so the party’s origin, how
they became inspectors, and any earlier cases are unknown.

campaigns/jakedm.title: JakeDM's Campaign (2023)
campaigns/jakedm.content:
JakeDM’s Campaign (2023)
A 2023 campaign DM’d by Jake, running a mercenary crew through a doppelganger-infiltrated bank heist,
an accidental city-leveling catastrophe, a refugee flight, and a magic-carpet death race — six sessions
recorded so far, the last ending on an unresolved cliffhanger. One session in the middle is a disconnected
one-shot DM’d by Pat instead of Jake, almost certainly mislabeled into this slug (see Interlude, below).
Shape of the campaign: main arc + a mislabeled interlude

Main arc — Heist, Firestorm, and the Carpet Race (Sep–Nov 2023). The party, a band of mercenaries
raised together by an unnamed “adopted father” benefactor, is hired by Mitch Copperhead to rob a
bank in Lidurithal and kill its doppelganger head of guard, Cadillac. The heist succeeds in
part — the Dyson Dynamo is recovered, but Cadillac escapes — and the party’s own fire magic,
amplified by the soul-charged Dynamo, levels an entire city. The survivors flee as refugees, flying
ahead of the column to Lutathal to enter the Magic Carpet Race, pick up a new party member
(Gang), and draw the attention of a planar law-enforcement agency hunting the Dynamo — ending
session 6 on a fresh cliffhanger as a demon rises through the city streets.
Interlude — Hawthorne and the Tomb of Horrors (session 3), DM’d by Pat. 2023-10-08
is titled “Copperhead the Doppelganger” and slotted into this campaign’s session list, but its content
has nothing to do with the heist arc: it’s run by Pat, not Jake, and follows two entirely different
characters — Jace Gandolfini (Jake) and Sarkhan Vol (Nutty), wizard-professors at Hawthorne
College — setting out after the Tomb of Horrors. No on-mic connection to the main arc exists. Treated
here as a stand-alone interlude rather than invented continuity.

The party (main arc)
Character names and even classes are inconsistently stated across sessions (several PCs are never named
on mic at all); see each PC page’s own “Unresolved” section for specifics.

Pat — Pat’s Wizard, a tiefling wood mage with a prehensile tail; later described as a sorcerer with
a luck-dragon familiar named Randy
Donnie — Colt Hopper, a grippli (frog-folk) gunslinger, later named Donovan; also fields a second
character, the witch Aisling
Connor — Jim Jones (nickname only), a human/cursed Oracle
Rich — Richard Findelberg, an android wizard/crafter
Nutty — Seabreeze, a Strix archer also described as a Druid
Ozan — Frankie, a Paladin/Bard with very high Charisma
Jess — Jess’s Witch, a witch (later revealed to be a changeling) who owns the folding boat Nessie
therealvossi (“Ty”) — Gang, a half-orca bar bouncer recruited into the party in session 6

Timeline

2023-09-12 — Mitch Copperhead hires the party
to rob a bank in Lidurithal and kill Cadillac; they infiltrate the city, dodge the guard, and
enter the bank just as a rival crew tunnels in using giant burrowing creatures — cliffhanger.
2023-10-01 — A three-way vault brawl against Cadillac’s crew;
the party recovers the loot and the Dyson Dynamo, but Cadillac escapes under cover of his own
wizard’s Darkness spell.
2023-10-08 — Interlude, DM’d by Pat: [[Jace
Gandolfini]] and Sarkhan Vol decipher a cursed map and prepare to set out for the Tomb of Horrors.
2023-10-15 — An ambush by Copperhead’s doppelganger caravan
turns into a magical firestorm when the Dynamo mirrors the party’s own fire spell across the city of
Godoy, killing roughly 90% of its population; the party loots the ruins and covers its tracks.
2023-10-24 — The party flees Godoy with the refugee
column, flies ahead to Lutathal to enter the Magic Carpet Race, scries on Cadillac’s purge plans,
and falls out with a carpet-shop sponsor, Greg.
2023-11-28 — Planar investigators from the
TIU confront the party over the Dynamo and mark them as suspects; the party recruits Gang,
bait-and-switches a race carpet, and the session ends as a demon rises through the city streets.

Major threads
Resolved

The bank heist for Mitch Copperhead — bank robbed, Dynamo recovered, though Cadillac escaped
2023-10-01
Copperhead’s doppelganger caravan ambush — caravan killed/burned, Copperhead himself killed
2023-10-15

Dangling / open

Cadillac himself survives, now plotting to purge changelings near the king
2023-10-24
The Dyson Dynamo’s soul-harvesting nature and how the party means to recharge it going forward
Covering up the destruction of Godoy (~90% mortality) — no in-fiction consequences yet
The TIU’s manhunt — the party is now flagged as suspects in the Dynamo’s disappearance
2023-11-28
The Magic Carpet Race (the Rug Mandela) — entered via a bait-and-switch carpet, race not yet run
The demon rising through the city streets — brand-new cliffhanger, completely unresolved
Richard’s indentured servitude to the rug shop, bartered away to avoid paying for a carpet — never
revisited on-mic after session 5
The Tomb of Horrors expedition (interlude) — map deciphered, party preparing to depart; no further
session has picked it back up

Unresolved
Whether session 3’s Hawthorne/Tomb of Horrors content belongs to this campaign at all, or is simply
mislabeled with the “jakedm” slug, is never clarified — it shares no characters, DM, or plot with the
other five sessions. Several locations across the main arc (Lidurithal vs. Godoy) may be the same
city under different transcribed names; see each place page’s own Unresolved section.

campaigns/ravenloft.title: Ravenloft (2022–2023)
campaigns/ravenloft.content:
Ravenloft (2022–2023)
Pat ran the party through the classic 1980s Curse of Strahd/Ravenloft module (confirmed by Pat
OOC as the original 1984 TSR adventure, not the 5e remake)
2023-01-30 @ 05:36:35,
2023-03-18 @ 00:33:00. A mysterious letter and dinner
invitation lure the party into the fogbound land of Barovia, ruled by the vampire lord
Strahd von Zarovich. After one scene-setting session in the village, the remaining seven sessions are
an almost continuous dungeon crawl through Castle Ravenloft itself, with the party never leaving the
castle again.
The recorded campaign ends mid-dungeon, unresolved: Strahd is still alive, one former party member is
lost in the Astral Plane, and the party’s last on-screen action is splitting up to chase a screaming noise
toward a glowing tower. The group’s next recorded sessions move on to a different, unrelated campaign
(JakeDM’s), so it’s unclear from the transcripts whether Ravenloft was ever formally finished or simply
left behind.
The party

Todd (Todd Stone) — played by Nutty — human fighter, dual-shield tank, carries the party’s torches.
The most consistently-named and stable PC across the whole campaign. See Todd Stone.
Jacques Luceau (aliases: Woo-woo, Wu, JB) — played by Jake — a Vanara (monkey-folk) monk, flurry of
blows, later elemental/flaming fists. See Jacques Luceau.
Raven / Donovan — played by Donnie — a human witch with a brain-hungry zoog familiar. Dies near
Strahd’s coffin and rises as his vampire thrall, later revealed to have secretly betrayed the party
before being defeated and lost into the Astral Plane. See Raven.
Xarthax (heard as Zyrtax/Zarthax/Zarafax) — played by Rich — an android arcane caster, immune to
necrotic damage, fear, aging, and mind-affecting effects. Note: session 1 instead describes “Rich’s
character” as an unnamed drow bard and a separate absent “Jeff’s character” as a mage; it’s unclear
whether either is meant to be Xarthax, who appears from session 2 onward. See Xarthax.
Alumbra (heard as: Ulumbra, Alhambra, Olumbra, Lulu) — played by Jess — a ninja/rogue with a katana,
sneak attack, and a handy haversack (later destroyed). See Alumbra.
Ozan’s alchemist (heard as: Zendrick, Lobel, Nadi, “Woo”/“Wubu Tang”) — played by Ozan — an
alchemist/investigator who disables traps, brews potions, and shares them mid-fight. See
Ozan’s Alchemist.

Timeline

2022-12-06 — A shared prophetic nightmare and a forged plea
letter draw the party into the mists around Barovia; they meet Ismark and Irina Indirovich, shelter in
the village church, get a tarot reading from Madame Eva, and arrive at Castle Ravenloft’s doors by
carriage.
2022-12-18 — Strahd greets the party for
dinner and vanishes after being hit with a thrown roll; the party fights skeletons, finds the cursed
Tome of Strahd, and falls through a trap door into a flooded dungeon level.
2022-12-26 — A poison-gas trap gets set on
fire and burns for most of the session; the party meets the pet-murdering armor Bartholomew and Jake
claims a shapeshifting magic sword from the flames.
2023-01-30 — The party invents “piss coat” to bypass warded
bars, clears the catacombs beneath the castle (killing a banshee wife and a vampire bride of Strahd),
learns Strahd’s Tatiana backstory, identifies the Sun Sword’s blade, and loses Donnie’s witch to
vampirism at Strahd’s coffin.
2023-02-12 — Donovan (now a vampire thrall) flees as mist;
the party opens Strahd’s empty coffin and teleports into a brutal boss fight with Strahd himself, who
dominates several PCs before escaping as mist.
2023-03-12 — A riddle-trapped treasure room animates two iron golems;
the party nearly loses Alumbra to poison and a critical fumble before grinding both golems down.
2023-03-18 — Donovan is revealed
to have secretly turned traitor; the party defeats him and a demon, then accidentally flings Donovan
into the Astral Plane while trying to contain his mist form. A later ghost ambush in a dining hall
nearly wipes the party.
2023-03-18 — A short continuation: Todd explores
alone, the party levels to 7 and handles character-build bookkeeping, and the session (and the
campaign’s recorded run) ends early when the battle map breaks.

Major threads
Resolved

The dinner invitation / tarot prophecy — overtaken by events once the party committed to the castle.
The basement’s rumored magic item — the shapeshifting sword, later identified as the Sun Sword’s
blade — 2022-12-26,
2023-01-30.
Petrifying wards guarding Strahd’s crypt — bypassed with “piss coat”
2023-01-30 @ 04:25:30.
The riddle/golem trap room — both golems destroyed
2023-03-12.
Donovan’s betrayal, as a live threat — defeated and removed from play (flung into the Astral Plane)
2023-03-18.

Dangling / open

Kolyan Indirovich’s disappearance and Irina Indirovich’s vampiric bite — never followed up on
once the party moved on to the castle.
The “tool of evil” from Madame Eva’s tarot prophecy — never explicitly identified; possibly the Sun
Sword, but this is never confirmed on-screen.
The Sun Sword’s missing hilt — never recovered.
Strahd von Zarovich himself — still alive and un-fought-to-a-finish as of the last session.
Donovan’s fate in the Astral Plane — had two hours to find a resting place or be destroyed
forever; never resolved on-screen.
The stolen copy of the Tome of Strahd — taken by a group of ghosts who captured (rather than killed)
the party; never recovered.
The tower with the pulsing red glass “heart” — discovered but unexplored at the very end of the
campaign’s recorded run.

Unresolved
Whether this campaign was ever actually finished, abandoned, or picked up again off-mic is not something
the transcripts say — the recorded sessions simply stop here and the group’s next recorded games are a
different campaign (JakeDM’s).

campaigns/the-gang.title: The Gang (2019–2021)
campaigns/the-gang.content:
The Gang (2019–2021)
A long-running, free-wheeling homebrew campaign DM’d by Pat, running from October 2019 through at least
November 2021 (the latest recorded session). The table calls it simply “the campaign” — “The Gang” is
this wiki’s label for it. Tonally it swings from dungeon-crawl pulp (pyramids, sphinxes, golems) to
cosmic/planar horror (the Abyss, the Nexus, Lovecraftian artifacts) to outright slapstick (urination as
a puzzle solution, a hat that renames people “Steve”). Pat has stated at the table that the party has
previously fought in an Orc War, run a casino heist, killed a lich, and been trapped in a Titan’s pocket
“fish tank” universe — all backstory from before this wiki’s transcript coverage begins.
Across its recorded span the party acquires, loses, or gets stuck with a long chain of reality-bending
artifacts (a planeshifting ship, the Apocalypse Box, a Ring of the Hive Mind, a newborn god),
gets yanked into the Abyss and back out, and survives several player-character deaths — almost always,
per Pat’s own observation, “from a cursed item turning players against each other,” not from monsters
2020-03-24 @ 03:23:59.
Shape of the campaign: two arcs + an interlude
Character names, classes, and even species change substantially over the recorded timespan, with real
gaps of months between sessions. This wiki splits the record into two loose arcs plus one outlier
one-shot, rather than assume continuity the transcripts don’t support:

Arc I — The Ship (Oct 2019 – Apr 2020). The party raids a pyramid, steals a mage’s
planeshifting/blood-fueled ship, gets dragged through the Abyss, Hell, and the Feywild, and ends up
raising a newborn god. Core cast: Tick-Tick (Jake), Mori Yoshinari (Donnie, the ship’s
captain), Dread Pirate Bobbert (Rich), Ozan’s bard/fey character (see Kurt Furbane), and
Nutty’s healer (unexpectedly possessed by a demon for several sessions).
Interlude — The Kidnap Job (Sep 2020), DM’d by Ozan. A single one-shot heist session with an
entirely different cast of goblins and a dwarf monk, run by Ozan instead of Pat while Pat played a
PC. See 2020-09-28. Not clearly connected to either
main arc; treated here as a stand-alone interlude.
Arc II — The Nexus (Oct–Nov 2021). After an ~18-month real-world gap, the party (now playing
Alexander, Fish, Miss Cleo, Nutty’s fire sorcerer, and Jess’s magus) is deep in an
unrelated-looking cult/portal-hopping plot that ends with them trapped in a planar prison called
the Nexus. Whether/how this connects to Arc I is never stated in the transcripts.

The party (by arc)
Arc I

Jake — Tick-Tick, later Paladin of Pelor; earlier an unnamed earth-gliding shapeshifter in the
pyramid session
Donnie — Mori Yoshinari / Donovan, the ship’s captain, bonded to an enslaved air elemental
Rich — Dread Pirate Bobbert, wizard
Ozan — bard/fey performer, see Kurt Furbane; killed and True-Resurrected mid-arc
Nutty — healer/alchemist, unknowingly possessed by a demon for several sessions
Ryan (Rawntrail) — Obadiah Jones, Loxodon cleric, joins partway through

Arc II

Jake — Alexander, android
Donnie — Fish (Donovan), alchemist; piloted by Rich when Donnie was absent
Rich — his own unnamed tank/healer character, and stand-in pilot for Fish
Ozan — Miss Cleo
Nutty — fire sorcerer, “the character formerly known as Ari”
Jess — unnamed elf magus/dhampir with a bat familiar

Timeline

2019-10-15 — The party fights through the
pyramid’s “Tests of the Pharaoh,” destroys clay golems, and is ambushed by shadow-doubles of
themselves before a half-finished boss fight against an awakened, staff-wielding figure.
2020-01-20 — Looting the dead mage’s ship,
the party accidentally triggers its plane-shift crystal, strands itself on a new continent, and has
an air elemental permanently bound to the ship so it can fly.
2020-01-28 — Shopping, scrying a hunter-paladin, and a
doomed feast in an isolated mountain village end with the ship accidentally yanked into the Abyss.
2020-03-16 — A Whimsy Wall roll conjures the
Apocalypse Box, which curses Jake to carry and (daily) risk opening it.
2020-03-24 — A demon secretly possessing
Nutty kills Ozan and then Jake; Jake dies and is reborn a Paladin of Pelor, lifting the box’s curse.
2020-03-25 — The party finally escapes Hell/the Abyss via the
ship, after a side-dungeon demon fight, and lands (not quite safely) in the Feywild instead of home.
2020-04-06 — Trapped in an escalating monster
trial, the party frees a frozen Loxodon cleric (Obadiah Jones) while a demon drags Jake into the
Ethereal Plane.
2020-04-13 — The party adopts a newborn god, then kills a
glabrezu demon disguised as a paladin mid-knighting-ceremony, leveling to 12.
2020-09-28 — One-shot interlude, Ozan DMing: the
party (as goblins and a dwarf monk) infiltrates a mansion banquet to kidnap a goblin, Littlepen.
2021-10-19 — A talking Sphinx painting’s riddles open
the way into a Nexus-portal complex; the party scouts and steps through into a frozen plane.
2021-11-02 — The party fights free of a frost
giant and golems on the frozen plane, loots a haul of magic items, and learns they’re trapped in a
planar prison called the Nexus, with no way back.

Major threads
Resolved

Escaping Hell/the Abyss with the ship — 2020-03-25
The Apocalypse Box’s compulsion curse on Jake (lifted when he died and was reborn a Paladin) —
2020-03-24
The demon possessing Nutty — banished the same session
Ozan’s death and True Resurrection — died 2020-03-24, confirmed alive again by 2020-04-06
The kidnapping of Littlepen — 2020-09-28

Dangling / open

The Apocalypse Box itself was never destroyed, only stopped being Jake’s problem
The green death-bubble sealing the Isle of Death, and the lich it may be tied to
The freed djinn the party keeps failing to locate/scry
The Church of St. Cuthbert’s manhunt for Mori Yoshinari
The newborn god-baby’s upbringing and future religion
Jake’s interrupted duel to the death at Clydewell
The miasma death-cloud and the never-found “Miasmic Cloud Monitoring Agency”
The Grimson Knights cult and “Brother Felhorn”
Escaping the Nexus — the campaign’s last recorded session ends on this cliffhanger

Unresolved
The exact relationship between Arc I and Arc II — whether Arc II’s cast are new characters in a new
campaign thread, or a direct continuation nobody explained on-mic — is never stated in the transcripts.

factions/aspis-corporation.title: Aspis Corporation
factions/aspis-corporation.content:
A faction providing security and guests for a lavish mansion banquet in the one-shot kidnap job session;
likely the table’s name for the Pathfinder Society’s “Aspis Consortium.” Hostile to the party after the
kidnapping.
History

Hosts/attends the banquet where Littlepen is a guest
2020-09-28 @ 00:08:48.
An Aspis Corporation guard engages the fleeing party during the kidnapping’s getaway, landing hard hits
on Jake, Donnie, and Rich 2020-09-28 @ 02:27:01.

factions/college-of-turgeth.title: College of Turgeth
factions/college-of-turgeth.content:
A magic college in Turgeth specializing in aberration and self-protection magic, likened to “Notre
Dame” and said to exist on every continent. Secretly the true source of the drug Maka.
History

Riggs’s Widow reveals the college secretly supplies Maka, worth ~75,000 gp/week
2025-03-31 @ 00:24:08-00:24:19, @ 00:25:03.
Jake establishes its specialty as aberration/self-protection magic
2025-03-31 @ 00:32:02-00:32:34.

DM notes (spoiler)
The college’s drug pipeline is confirmed by Jake as true (not a prisoner’s lie), but the party has not
yet investigated it directly — see College of Turgeth Drug Pipeline.

factions/grimson-knights.title: Grimson Knights
factions/grimson-knights.content:
A cult whose abandoned underground complex the party explores in Arc II, found via red robes, a ledger of
cult expenses, and desiccated bodies with their hearts magically removed. Planning a ritual gathering to
welcome a new lord, Brother Felhorn.
History

The party finds the cult’s hastily-abandoned living quarters, robes, and a ledger of expenses
2021-10-19 @ 00:07:22–00:09:24.
A recovered note announces a ritual gathering in a graveyard under the next full moon to welcome “our
new lord and life, Brother Felhorn” 2021-10-19 @ 00:14:57.
Several desiccated, heart-removed bodies are found preserved rather than killed violently, implying
ritual victims 2021-10-19 @ 00:18:33.

Unresolved
The cult members themselves and Brother Felhorn are never found or confronted in the recorded sessions.

factions/tiu.title: TIU
factions/tiu.content:
A planar law-enforcement organization out of the city of Chrome, whose agents astral-project rather than
travel physically. Hunting the Dyson Dynamo and now the party, whom it has marked as suspects.
History

Investigators Thornshade and Iron Soul confront the party over the Dyson Dynamo, warning it “could
unravel the fabric of reality” 2023-11-28
@ 00:37:54–00:38:31.
Thornshade is defeated in a brawl with Gang, shows his real badge, and explains the Dynamo harvests
souls @ 01:01:49–01:12:08.
Marks the party as suspects regardless of Donnie’s bluff denying any knowledge of the Dynamo, then
leaves after a gold-compensation offer is rebuffed @ 00:39:10–00:40:15, @ 01:14:51–01:18:33.

Unresolved
Thornshade vows to return; no later session has done so yet.

items/apocalypse-box.title: Apocalypse Box
items/apocalypse-box.content:
A small black wooden box, the third major artifact the party stumbles into during Arc I. Once per day its
bearer can pull one non-magical item from it, but there’s a 50% chance of instead unleashing horrific
monsters that linger for about a week. Can only be destroyed by having its bearer survive three waves of
its summoned monsters and then tricking a gold dragon into crushing it (which kills the dragon too).
History

Conjured into Ozan’s hands by a near-maximum d1000 Whimsy Wall roll
2020-03-16 @ 00:18:15.
Everyone who examines it must make a DC 30 will save; Jake fails and is magically compelled to seize and
guard it from everyone else, including by violence
2020-03-16 @ 00:21:18–00:27:47.
Ozan identifies it via a knowledge check as the legendary Apocalypse Box and explains its powers before
ceding it to Jake 2020-03-16 @ 00:28:35.
Two openings nearly summon six Shoggoths each (CR19) before a third reroll produces a bottle of scotch
instead 2020-03-16 @ 00:41:19–00:43:48.
Donnie reveals the destruction method: three survived monster-waves, then a gold dragon crushing it
2020-03-16 @ 00:44:54.
Jake’s compulsion to open it daily, under an increasingly hard will save, becomes a life-threatening
crisis; the party considers killing him to stop it
2020-03-24 @ 00:30:49–00:39:46.
The curse ends when Jake dies and is reborn a Paladin of Pelor — he is “no longer compelled to
carry/open the Apocalypse Box” 2020-03-24
@ 02:39:50.
Deliberately left unexamined and forgotten in someone’s bag going forward
2020-03-25 @ 02:45:46.
Jake dares Pat (the DM, in-game as a bit) to open it; it turns out to contain only Pat’s own wallet, a
joke 2020-04-13 @ 01:25:49.

Unresolved
The box itself is never destroyed — only its curse on its bearer is lifted. Its ultimate fate is not
addressed again in the recorded sessions.

items/boots-of-haste.title: Boots of Haste
items/boots-of-haste.content:
Enchanted boots granting 6th-level haste once per week.
History

Gained: looted by Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) from the slain Fugly (killed by Nutty; nicknamed
“the captain” mid-fight — see The Guard Captain) 2025-03-31 @ 02:48:42,
identified as Boots of Haste @ 02:49:34.
Used: Rich activates the boots and goes ethereal to fly after the Boot’s departing ship
2025-03-31 @ 02:58:23-03:02:43, spotting the Boot himself as he flies
through the warehouse @ 03:09:40-03:10:13.

items/dyson-dynamo.title: Dyson Dynamo
items/dyson-dynamo.content:
A bronze, diamond-shaped artifact built by “a mad scientist” that harvests “just and unjust souls” to
grow in power, crosses planes, and reacts unpredictably to strong magical damage. Gained: bank vault,
episode 1. Used: triggered a citywide firestorm, episode 4. Lost: never — the party still carries it as
of episode 6, now hunted by the TIU.
History

Named as the heist’s target in the vault, “the dynamic dominum”; glimpsed being hauled toward the bank
by giant burrowing creatures 2023-09-12 @ 02:17:01,
@ 04:15:29.
Found in the vault chest as a glowing blue orb, confirmed via Knowledge Arcana to match the mission’s
target 2023-10-01 @ 03:59:31–03:59:37.
Dropped by its doppelganger carrier when killed by Nutty; charged with captured souls from the bank
heist, it reacts to Pat’s ongoing fire-spell damage by rolling to “react” and, on a near-maximum result,
mirrors the spell across the entire city of Godoy, killing roughly 90% of the population
2023-10-15 @ 00:36:05, @ 00:56:37–00:56:59.
Examined drained, warm to the touch, one valve open; Ozan’s knowledge-planes check says it exists on
another plane as well, and Jess’s follow-up planes/arcana/engineering check (a 30, explicitly “not a
natural 20”) confirms it’s crossed planes, likely siphoning souls elsewhere
2023-10-24 @ 00:19:10–00:22:38.
Hunted by TIU investigators, who identify it as the “Dyson Dynamo” and warn it “could unravel the
fabric of reality”; Donnie’s bluff denying any knowledge of it doesn’t sway Thornshade, who marks the
party as suspects regardless 2023-11-28
@ 00:37:54–00:40:15.

Unresolved
Whether “the dynamic dominum” (episode 1), “the Dynamo”/“the device” (episodes 2, 4–5), and the “Dyson
Dynamo” (episode 6) are definitively the same artifact is implied by plot continuity but never restated
explicitly in a single session.

items/folding-boat-nessie.title: Folding Boat Nessie
items/folding-boat-nessie.content:
Jess’s folding boat, a box that transforms via command word into a 10-ft rowboat or a 24-ft ship with
cabin, mast, and sail (holds 15). Gained: already owned by Jess’s character before episode 1 (a recurring
item across her characters, per her own running joke). Used: river mooring/shelter and air travel out of
Godoy, episode 5.
History

Jess jokes that she’s gotten a folding boat “a couple times” before and never used it — implying it’s a
pre-existing character item rather than a reward won this session; a separate whimsy-table roll taken
around the same time turns her into a weasel instead
2023-09-12 @ 01:57:49, @ 02:20:47.
Unfolded on land near the riverbank into full ship form (cabin, anchor) as an overnight shelter for the
refugee party, then floated out onto the river; named “Nessie” when Ozan asks for the boat’s name
2023-10-24 @ 00:43:07–00:45:49.
Flown roughly twelve hours to Lutathal after Pat casts Fly on it and hands control to his familiar,
Randy @ 01:04:35–01:17:11.

items/golden-ticket-to-the-devil.title: Golden Ticket to the Devil
items/golden-ticket-to-the-devil.content:
A one-way pass to the devil holding Riggs’s soul, hidden in a locker and sought by Riggs’s Widow.
Not retrieved by anyone during session 3.
History

Described by Riggs’s Widow as her goal in engineering her own capture
2025-03-31 @ 00:19:45, @ 00:20:31.

Unresolved
The ticket’s location, beyond “a locker,” and who currently holds it are unknown; see
Golden Ticket to the Devil (quest).

items/locate-portal-sextant.title: Locate Portal Sextant
items/locate-portal-sextant.content:
A brass, sextant-like “locate portal” device found in Arc II’s cult complex, with seven glass-marble
slots. Each installed jewel permanently tracks the location of a linked Nexus portal. Distinct from the
unrelated Arc I Planar Sextant aboard the party’s ship.
History

Found by Jess in a desk drawer in the sealed Nexus-portal room, with only one of seven jewel slots
filled 2021-10-19 @ 01:25:33.
Identified by Rich as a permanent locate-portal device needing seven jewels total
2021-10-19 @ 02:39:05.
A new red gem, suspected to key a fiery plane, is recovered from a glowing flag on the frost giant’s
mountaintop 2021-11-02 @ 02:03:16.
Confirmed unable to get the party back out of the Nexus — they must advance through the chain of
gem-keyed portals instead 2021-11-02 @ 02:30:02.

Unresolved
How many of the seven jewel slots remain to be filled, and what plane each corresponds to, is unresolved
at the end of the recorded sessions.

items/maka.title: Maka
items/maka.content:
The drug flooding Turgeth, secretly supplied by the College of Turgeth rather than street
dealers, worth roughly 75,000 gold a week.
History

Revealed by Riggs’s Widow to be secretly supplied by the College of Turgeth
2025-03-31 @ 00:24:08, @ 00:24:19.
An earlier mention of a street drug called “Rama” may refer to the same drug, misheard
2025-03-31 @ 00:43:47.

Unresolved
Whether “Maka” and “Rama” are the same drug heard two different ways, or two distinct drugs, is unclear.

items/nutty's-tail-weapon.title: Nutty's Tail Weapon
items/nutty's-tail-weapon.content:
Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice)‘s bladed tail, treated mechanically as a scimitar for an extra
attack.
History

Jake reminds Nutty the weapon exists, having been forgotten about
2025-03-31 @ 01:28:59.
Used to finish off Fugly in combination with a shocking-grasp touch attack (“Washashaka”)
2025-03-31 @ 02:46:05-02:48:22.

items/planar-sextant.title: Planar Sextant
items/planar-sextant.content:
A rare, touch-activated planar navigation device recovered aboard the looted ship, paired with a
gold-bound crystal that performs the actual plane shift. Nine discrete settings; the party never fully
mapped what each one does. Distinct from the later, unrelated Locate Portal Sextant found in Arc II.
History

Found in the ship’s helm room alongside a gold-bound crystal emanating conjuration/divination magic
2020-01-20 @ 00:17:25–00:33:43.
Donnie touches the crystal directly while experimenting with the sextant’s settings, triggering an
accidental plane shift 2020-01-20 @ 01:02:51.
Position 7 is established as triggering plane travel when the crystal is touched (with a helmet),
powered by blood sacrifice; position 9 shows an unrecognized blinking symbol
2020-01-28 @ 03:40:30.
Activates on its own overnight, dragging the ship into the first layer of the Abyss
2020-01-28 @ 03:40:30–03:45:48.
Donnie resets the navigation settings from memory to jump the ship out of Hell, landing the party in the
Feywild instead of home 2020-03-25 @ 02:31:40–02:36:13.

Unresolved
The exact mapping of settings 1–6 and 8 was never established in play; the mechanism by which the crystal
activated itself unprompted is not explained.

items/revelation-crystals.title: Revelation Crystals
items/revelation-crystals.content:
A pair of gems offered by a skeleton child in a shared dream, which reveal hidden truths; each left a
brand on the back of its recipient’s hand. Appears only in the Pat-DM’d interlude session; see
2023-10-08 and jakedm Unresolved.
History

Offered to and accepted by Jace Gandolfini and Sarkhan Vol in a shared nightmare
2023-10-08 @ 01:55:54–01:57:33.
Sarkhan uses his to dispel the cursed Tomb of Horrors map’s illusion @ 02:01:41.

items/ring-of-protection-+1.title: Ring of Protection +1
items/ring-of-protection-+1.content:
A ring granting +1 AC.
History

Gained/given: Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice) gives this ring to Ozone, raising his AC
2025-03-31 @ 03:19:55.

Unresolved
Where Nutty’s character originally got the ring is not stated.

items/ring-of-the-hive-mind.title: Ring of the Hive Mind
items/ring-of-the-hive-mind.content:
A magical signet ring that telepathically links wearers to a hive mind’s shared knowledge and senses,
while the wearer is conscious.
History

Taken off an unconscious intruder caught breaking into the party’s ship by Jake
2020-01-20 @ 00:01:12.
Identified by Nutty with a natural 20 Knowledge: Arcana check
2020-01-20 @ 00:04:19.

Unresolved
Who else is connected to the hive mind, or whether they’re now aware the party has one of their members’
rings, is never addressed.
Exactly when/how the ring ends up with Nutty is unclear. The timestamp previously cited here
(@ 01:01:12 in 2020-01-20) is actually an
unrelated scene (the party experimenting with the ship’s planar crystal/sextant) — no “hands it to Nutty”
moment was found near that timestamp, or elsewhere in the session. Nutty is the one who identifies the
ring with a natural 20 Knowledge: Arcana check, which may be the source of the assumption that he kept it.

items/sun-sword.title: Sun Sword
items/sun-sword.content:
A legendary magic longsword, +3 and dealing bonus damage against vampires and undead within 30 feet.
Shapeshifts into whatever weapon its wielder imagines. Its blade and hilt were deliberately separated long
ago by a powerful magician trying to destroy it; only the blade has been recovered, and the campaign ends
with the hilt still lost.
History

Found as an unidentified shapeshifting sword lying in the middle of an active fire trap in the flooded
basement; Jake braves the flames to claim it, and it takes the form of a glowing blue
rapier when he imagines one
2022-12-26 @ 03:58:19–03:59:58.
Used to pry open Strahd’s coffin, referred to in the moment as “Dawnblade”
2023-02-12 @ 00:42:03.
Found buried with Sergei von Zarovich’s body in the catacombs is a second piece: the Sun Sword’s own
blade, alongside magic armor 2023-01-30 @ 03:53:07–03:54:21.
A Spellcraft check identifies the sword Jake has been carrying since the gas-trap
session as the Sun Sword’s blade — +3 vs. undead with 10 bonus damage vs. vampires within 30 feet — but
confirms its hilt was separated from the blade long ago and remains lost
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.

Unresolved
Whether the “shapeshifting sword” found in the fire trap and the blade found in Sergei’s crypt are
literally the same physical object, or two related pieces, is not entirely disentangled in the notes —
both are identified as “the Sun Sword’s blade” by the piss-coat session, and Jake is the one carrying it
throughout. The sword’s hilt is never found in the recorded sessions.

items/tome-of-strahd.title: Tome of Strahd
items/tome-of-strahd.content:
A cursed, dark-magic-laced grimoire — Strahd von Zarovich’s own journal of poems, stories, and diary
entries — said to grant power to readers but risk madness. Contains several torn-out pages.
History

Found hidden under the mattress in Strahd’s personal chamber; identified by Xarthax via Knowledge
(History) as a dangerous, sought-after artifact. Xarthax reads the (safe) early pages
2022-12-18 @ 02:09:47–02:17:02.
Its missing, torn-out pages are flagged by Xarthax as valuable/dangerous and worth hunting down — never
pursued in the recorded sessions
2022-12-18 @ 02:41:23–02:41:54.
Stolen from the party (last carried by Donnie/Donovan) when an earlier, less lethal group of
ghosts captures and ages the party instead of killing them
2023-03-18 @ 00:34:16–00:35:05.

Unresolved
The book is never recovered after being stolen by the ghosts; its torn-out pages are never found or
explained.

items/wand-of-memory-lapse.title: Wand of Memory Lapse
items/wand-of-memory-lapse.content:
Pat’s wand; forces a DC 17 Will save to erase a target’s recent memory. Gained: already owned at the
start of episode 1. Used: twice on Mary to erase an awkward encounter.
History

Used twice on Mary: once to erase her memory of a gangbang-joke misunderstanding at her door, once
again after Connor insults her 2023-09-12
@ 02:56:41, @ 03:06:06.

items/whoop-whoop-whistle.title: Whoop Whoop Whistle
items/whoop-whoop-whistle.content:
Ozone’s magic item: a whistle with a knockout effect plus 1d4 lightning damage.
History

Jake reminds Ozan the item exists, having been forgotten about
2025-03-31 @ 01:29:47-01:30:04.

DM notes (spoiler)
Jake plans to “remix” this item’s mechanics after the session
2025-03-31 @ 03:19:44.

npcs/andrew.title: Andrew
npcs/andrew.content:
A sphinx-like winged creature encountered alone by Rich in a hidden underwater chamber inside the pyramid,
offering to answer a question about the temple if Rich could solve a riddle.
History

Meets Rich after his rope snaps and sweeps him into a hidden chamber; offers a classic
truth-teller/liar riddle in exchange for answering a question about the temple
2019-10-15 @ 01:13:40.
Rich stalls and ultimately swims back against the current without answering
2019-10-15 @ 01:21:10.

Unresolved
Andrew is never seen again in the recorded sessions; whatever he knew about the temple was never learned.

npcs/bartholomew.title: Bartholomew
npcs/bartholomew.content:
A sentient, multi-personality suit of full plate armor found guarding a dusty servant’s-entrance room in
Castle Ravenloft. Documented in-world as “full plate armor of pet murder by committee” — each piece of
plate carries a different alignment, with only one personality active at a time. Hunts and electrocutes
pets, but can be talked down rather than fought.
History

Encountered by the party, alternating between a murderous “pet murder by committee” persona and a posh,
amnesiac one; claims to have blacked out roughly 25 years ago after being arrested for killing a snake
in a town 2022-12-26 @ 02:09:05–02:20:25.
Identified via Knowledge (Arcana) as “full plate armor of pet murder by committee”
2022-12-26 @ 02:16:56.
Talked down by the party rather than fought; relationship left non-hostile
2022-12-26 @ 02:20:52.

DM notes (spoiler)
Bartholomew’s backstory was given directly to the players in-character, but its truth and significance to
the wider plot was never confirmed by the DM
2022-12-26 @ 02:19:07–02:20:25.

npcs/cadillac.title: Cadillac
npcs/cadillac.content:
A fox-person crime boss and the city’s head guard, confirmed a doppelganger; marked kill-on-sight by
Mitch Copperhead for the bank job, but survives every encounter with the party so far. Leads a gang
marked with a green bee insignia.
History

Named kill-on-sight target of the heist by Mitch Copperhead, who first describes him as the city’s
head guard and a doppelganger 2023-09-12 @ 02:16:04;
later confirmed a doppelganger/changeling by Mary @ 03:02:24.
Leads his own crew looting the bank vault ahead of the party; grapples and nearly captures Pat; counters
his Magic Missile via an ally mage; kills his own unconscious ally “Big Sleepy” with an opportunistic
attack; escapes under cover of his own wizard’s Darkness spell
2023-10-01 @ 01:18:33, @ 02:49:08, @ 04:12:40.
Scried on by Pat for seven minutes; shown privately planning to purge and re-vet changelings near the
king now that most of Godoy’s changeling population is dead; his mage group’s sigil matches the
Lutathal city guards’ 2023-10-24 @ 00:49:09–00:54:54,
@ 01:25:59.

Unresolved
Whether the fox-person seen arguing with bank tellers early in episode 2 is Cadillac himself or a
separate NPC/Fish’s character is ambiguous in the transcript
2023-10-01 @ 00:20:15.

npcs/dex.title: Dex
npcs/dex.content:
Drunk dockworker at The Boot’s warehouse, secretly a lookout.
History

Gets high with Ozone (posing as “Mr. Vajidkas”), trading moonshine and cocaine for information
2025-03-31 @ 00:56:49.
Reveals the warehouse is finishing a shipment leaving that night, bound for “Rolesk”
2025-03-31 @ 00:58:50-00:59:19.
Fires a flare and pulls a gun, revealing himself as a lookout and triggering the warehouse firefight
2025-03-31 @ 01:05:14-01:06:02.

Unresolved
The ship’s destination, heard as “Rolesk,” is likely a mangled place name
2025-03-31 @ 00:59:19.

npcs/fugly.title: Fugly
npcs/fugly.content:
The Boot’s orc enforcer, wielding twin machetes. His goat-like horns are growing back into his own
skull, slowly driving him mad.
History

Confronts Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) alone deeper in the warehouse, named by Jake
2025-03-31 @ 01:39:02, @ 01:39:20.
Rich runs past rather than stopping to fight; Fugly’s follow-up attack misses
2025-03-31 @ 01:39:22-01:40:13.
Rich doubles back to fight him properly; Jake’s narration confirms it’s still the orc
2025-03-31 @ 01:41:11, @ 01:48:40.
Follows Rich down the stairs as Rich keeps chasing The Boot, and critically wounds him for 36
damage 2025-03-31 @ 01:52:32-01:53:30.
Flanked and killed by Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice) downstairs with a combined
weapon-and-shocking-grasp strike (“Washashaka”); Rich then loots his Boots of Haste from the
corpse 2025-03-31 @ 02:46:05-02:48:42.

Unresolved
Partway through the long fight, Rich and Nutty start calling this enemy “the captain”
2025-03-31 @ 01:43:49, @ 01:55:17, and the wiki previously tracked him as a
separate NPC, The Guard Captain. No second named enemy is ever introduced on mic, Jake narrates him as
“the orc” mid-fight @ 01:48:40, and he’s the one who follows Rich downstairs and whose corpse yields the
Boots of Haste — so this is almost certainly just Fugly, nicknamed “the captain” by the players once the
fight turned out to be much tougher than expected, not a distinct NPC. See The Guard Captain for the
remaining doubt.

npcs/greg.title: Greg
npcs/greg.content:
A carpet-shop owner and sponsor of the Magic Carpet Race in Lutathal; “it’s pronounced Greg” became a
running joke at the table.
History

Negotiates a race sponsorship deal with the party in exchange for 15% of winnings; the deal collapses
after Ozan jokingly offers Rich as collateral, and Rich threatens to burn the shop down
2023-10-24 @ 02:30:16–02:58:48, @ 03:10:05–03:12:57.
Cursed by Jess, compelling him to count every board in his shop, in retaliation for the collapsed deal
@ 03:15:01–03:18:00.
Referenced in session 6’s recap: the party nearly firebombed his shop; instead Frankie traded Richard
into indentured service rather than pay for a carpet
2023-11-28 @ 00:12:38–00:13:23.

npcs/irina-indirovich.title: Irina Indirovich
npcs/irina-indirovich.content:
Adopted daughter of the Burgomaster Kolyan Indirovich and sister of Ismark Indirovich. Bitten
twice by Strahd von Zarovich and slowly turning into a vampire — the crisis that draws the party to
Barovia in the first place.
History

Found barricaded in the family’s guest house, bitten twice by Strahd, casting no reflection
2022-12-06 @ 02:58:06, @ 02:57:51.
Refuses to be chained up for safety; Donnie’s Remove Curse has no effect on her
2022-12-06 @ 03:05:00, @ 03:08:25.
Orders the party off the family property alongside her brother
2022-12-06 @ 03:07:21.

Unresolved
Whether Irina ever fully turns into a vampire is never shown — she and her brother are not seen again
after the party leaves for Castle Ravenloft.

npcs/ismark-indirovich.title: Ismark Indirovich
npcs/ismark-indirovich.content:
Son of the missing Burgomaster Kolyan Indirovich and brother of Irina Indirovich. Wears a holy
ring his father gave him.
History

Meets the party at the Blood of the Vine tavern and confirms his father vanished eight days earlier
seeking outside help, and that neither of the party’s letters matches his father’s real handwriting
2022-12-06 @ 02:32:48–02:34:29.
Helps the party search his father’s office, then his sister’s guest house
2022-12-06 @ 02:44:57, @ 02:52:37.
Orders the party off the family property after they try to restrain his bitten sister
2022-12-06 @ 03:05:00–03:07:21.

Unresolved
Ismark is never seen again after the party is ordered off the property; his and Irina’s fate is not
followed up on in later sessions.

npcs/jerry.title: Jerry
npcs/jerry.content:
The inspectors’ teleporter operator/custodian. Apologetic, knits sweaters for his mother, refuses tips.
History

Returns to the office nursing a broken finger, courtesy of the new prisoner
2025-03-31 @ 00:05:58, @ 00:06:24.
Teleports the party to the Council chambers, then to the dockside warehouse
2025-03-31 @ 00:10:44, @ 00:40:27-00:42:21.

npcs/kolyan-indirovich.title: Kolyan Indirovich
npcs/kolyan-indirovich.content:
The Burgomaster of Barovia, father of Ismark Indirovich and adoptive father of
Irina Indirovich. Missing for roughly two weeks by the time the party arrives, having gone to seek
outside help.
History

His signed plea for help — describing his bitten daughter Irina — reaches the party
via a page 2022-12-06 @ 01:07:29.
His son Ismark confirms neither the plea nor the dinner invitation matches his father’s real handwriting
2022-12-06 @ 02:34:29.
His genuine handwriting is confirmed via a third letter found on a dead villager, implying a forger has
been producing near-identical letters 2022-12-06 @ 02:50:28.

Unresolved
Kolyan is never found in the recorded sessions — the party leaves Barovia for Castle Ravenloft without
resolving his disappearance.

npcs/littlepen.title: Littlepen
npcs/littlepen.content:
A goblin, the kidnapping target of the party’s one-shot heist job, attending a mansion banquet as a guest
of the Aspis Corporation.
History

Attends the mansion banquet as an Aspis Corporation guest; nearly exposed when guards sweep for an
unregistered goblin 2020-09-28 @ 00:17:30.
Sickened by the party’s poisoned soup along with roughly half the banquet
2020-09-28 @ 01:26:38.
Struck non-lethally and beaten unconscious by Nutty’s character and Jake under cover of darkness
2020-09-28 @ 02:09:53–02:20:27.
Successfully carried off and secured aboard the party’s getaway boat
2020-09-28 @ 03:19:14.

npcs/loren-fenn.title: Loren Fenn
npcs/loren-fenn.content:
Council archivist in Turgeth who meticulously timestamps every visit and comment.
History

Logs the party’s visit to the Council chambers and clears them to interrogate the prisoner,
Riggs’s Widow 2025-03-31 @ 00:11:58, @ 00:14:20.

Unresolved
Mentions a “Captain Elas” once; could not be confirmed as a real recurring name or a mishearing
2025-03-31 @ 00:12:48.

npcs/madame-eva.title: Madame Eva
npcs/madame-eva.content:
A gypsy fortune teller who leads a roving encampment outside the village of Barovia, and had foreseen the
party’s arrival.
History

Gives the party a tarot (Tarokka) reading: Death (transformation, not literal death — reassuring Todd,
who learns he actually dies decades later choking on a sausage), a reversed card of conflict, and the
Fool, plus a prophecy about “a tool of evil” protected by darkness
2022-12-06 @ 03:44:15–03:52:28.
The reading is cut short when Todd, handed Donnie’s water skin for a drink, mistakenly splashes her with
Donnie’s holy water instead
2022-12-06 @ 04:00:19.

DM notes (spoiler)
Pat confirmed OOC that the tarot draws for this reading were genuinely random, not pre-stacked
2022-12-06 @ 03:44:21.
Unresolved
The “tool of evil” from her prophecy is never explicitly identified on-screen — possibly the
Sun Sword, but this link is never confirmed in-fiction.

npcs/mary.title: Mary
npcs/mary.content:
The party’s contact for the bank job, an older woman staying above the Howling Hooters in
Lidurithal.
History

Gives the party the bank’s layout and guard patrol schedule, and confirms Cadillac is a
doppelganger; agrees to hide the party for the night
2023-09-12 @ 03:01:14–03:05:01.
Has her memory wiped twice by Pat with the Wand of Memory Lapse, first to erase an awkward
gangbang-joke encounter, then again after Connor insults her @ 02:56:41, @ 03:06:06. (A separate,
later memory-lapse spell, cast by Connor’s Jim Jones, targets a guard who had learned Mary’s
whereabouts, not Mary herself @ 03:36:31–03:36:52.)

npcs/mitch-copperhead.title: Mitch Copperhead
npcs/mitch-copperhead.content:
A dwarf mercenary recruiter who carries a two-handed axe and hires the party for the bank job in
Lidurithal. Revealed by Mary to be a doppelganger, and later turns out to be part of his own
caravan’s doppelganger crew.
History

Hires the party for the bank job, names Cadillac kill-on-sight, and is talked up from 5,000 to
8,000 gold by Ozan 2023-09-12 @ 02:12:06–02:17:57.
Sends his servant creature Gus (a large bulldog) to deliver the party’s gold payment, then drops the
party outside Lidurithal; the transcript doesn’t specify how Mitch himself departs
@ 02:19:46–02:32:53.
Confirmed a doppelganger by Mary @ 03:02:24.
Revealed mid-ambush, heard as “Copperbeard”/“Copperfield,” leading the caravan of doppelgangers
carrying the Dyson Dynamo; killed by Nutty and looted (nothing of value found) by Ozan
2023-10-15 @ 00:01:19, @ 00:36:05, @ 01:47:02.

Unresolved
The identification of the ep4 caravan leader as the same Copperhead from episode 1 is presumed from name
similarity and plot continuity but never stated explicitly on mic.

npcs/murph.title: Murph
npcs/murph.content:
A human prisoner found locked in a basement cell beneath Castle Ravenloft.
History

Freed by Ozan after Todd spends many rounds breaking down the
reinforced door to his cell
2022-12-26 @ 03:04:37.
Immediately steps on an undetected teleport trap and is zapped into a nearby flooded cell, requiring a
second rescue 2022-12-26 @ 03:07:18.
Mentions arriving at the castle “naked outside” and references a Baron’s invitation and drinking with
gypsies, echoing the party’s own entry into Barovia
2022-12-26 @ 04:08:17.

Unresolved
Murph’s fate after this session is not mentioned again in the recorded transcripts.

npcs/petrina-velikovna.title: Petrina Velikovna
npcs/petrina-velikovna.content:
A withered vampire bride of Strahd von Zarovich, found desiccated in a crypt in the catacombs beneath
Castle Ravenloft.
History

Accidentally awakened when Nutty pours his own blood into her mouth, not realizing what she is
2023-01-30 @ 03:15:51.
Knocked unconscious by Wu before she can fully transform, then beheaded; the party keeps her fanged
skull as a trophy 2023-01-30 @ 03:17:00–03:21:00.
Her defeat/death is what restores Jess’s character from the petrification caused by Strahd’s crypt wards
2023-01-30 @ 04:20:48.

Unresolved
Her name is inconsistently spelled/spoken across the session as “Patrina Velikovna,” “Petrina Velikovna,”
and “Iflishkova” — likely the same character referred to with two different names
2023-01-30 @ 02:19:40, @ 03:04:25.

npcs/pop-jack.title: Pop Jack
npcs/pop-jack.content:
A large air elemental captured and permanently, forcibly bound to the party’s ship to give it flight.
Screams constantly in Mori Yoshinari’s mind after he bonds with it as captain; controlled through
charisma-based pain/threat domination.
History

Summoned, bound, and fed into a brass framework over two days by a Neo enchantress for 100,000 gold
2020-01-20 @ 02:29:27–02:33:00.
Mori Yoshinari speaks the command word “Pop Jack” to permanently bond with it
2020-01-20 @ 02:44:28.
Piloted via charisma-based pain/threat control to fly the ship to a capital city
2020-01-20 @ 02:53:03.
The ship is kept permanently parked thirty feet up by this point in the campaign “to dodge time
wizards,” implying ongoing routine use of the elemental’s flight
2020-04-13 @ 01:01:11.

DM notes (spoiler)
Elemental language is called “Orin,” and most elementals (and some monstrous races) culturally view
elemental enslavement as abhorrent — a detail the party has been told in-game but which underscores the
moral weight of binding Pop Jack permanently
2020-01-20 @ 02:37:03.
Unresolved
Whether Pop Jack is ever freed, or remains bound to the ship through the rest of the recorded campaign, is
not addressed after Arc I.

npcs/riggs's-widow.title: Riggs's Widow
npcs/riggs's-widow.content:
The widow of Riggs, Turgeth’s former crime boss. Sentenced to death. Engineered her own capture by
the inspectors to get close to a hidden golden ticket.
History

Flirted into talking by Ozone in her holding cell 2025-03-31 @ 00:15:20.
Reveals her husband Riggs lost a bargain with a devil and was dragged to hell
2025-03-31 @ 00:17:41.
Admits she used The Boot to get captured and track the party back to their HQ, hunting the
Golden Ticket to the Devil — a one-way pass to confront the devil holding Riggs’s soul
2025-03-31 @ 00:19:45, @ 00:20:31.
Reveals the drug Maka is secretly supplied by the College of Turgeth, worth ~75,000 gp/week
2025-03-31 @ 00:24:08-00:24:19, @ 00:25:03.

Unresolved
Her name was never stated on mic in session 3.

npcs/riggs.title: Riggs
npcs/riggs.content:
Former crime boss of Turgeth, running the city’s drug trade before The Boot. Husband of
Riggs’s Widow. Cut a deal with a devil for manpower, lost, and was dragged to hell.
History

Established by Jake as the previous boss, “sucked back into hell” 2025-03-31 @ 00:02:38.
His widow reveals he lost a bargain with a devil and was dragged to hell for it
2025-03-31 @ 00:17:41.
The Golden Ticket to the Devil his widow seeks would be a one-way pass to confront that devil and
reunite with Riggs’s soul 2025-03-31 @ 00:20:31.

npcs/sasha-ivliskova.title: Sasha Ivliskova
npcs/sasha-ivliskova.content:
A banshee found in crypt #21 of the catacombs beneath Castle Ravenloft — revealed to be one of
Strahd von Zarovich’s wives.
History

Attacks the party when her crypt is opened 2023-01-30
@ 02:19:40.
Defeated after dealing roughly 79 damage over the fight; the party loots 3,300 gold and a signet ring
from her crypt 2023-01-30 @ 02:59:16.

npcs/sergei-von-zarovich.title: Sergei von Zarovich
npcs/sergei-von-zarovich.content:
Strahd von Zarovich’s brother, murdered by Strahd out of jealousy over a shared love,
Tatiana. His preserved body was interred in the catacombs beneath Castle Ravenloft with the blade of
the Sun Sword and a suit of magic armor.
History

His preserved body is found in crypt #13 of the catacombs, buried with the Sun Sword’s blade and magic
armor 2023-01-30 @ 03:50:41.
Holy water splashed on his body by Donnie creates a mind-link, revealing that he and Strahd both loved
Tatiana, and that Strahd murdered them both out of jealousy
2023-01-30 @ 04:00:19–04:10:16.
His body crumbles to dust once the mind-link ends
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.

DM notes (spoiler)
His backstory is the motive for Strahd’s long-standing grief and villainy — Pat frames the original 1984
module’s Strahd as a villain with real motivations and grief rather than a generic monster
2023-03-18 @ 00:33:00–00:33:48.

npcs/sir-holton-albright.title: Sir Holton Albright
npcs/sir-holton-albright.content:
A paladin, “the Fiend Slayer,” being knighted and anointed at a temple ceremony the party crashes while
claiming to represent a far-off church of Pelor. Revealed mid-ritual to have been possessed/replaced by a
glabrezu demon.
History

Introduced as the honoree of a lavish knighting ceremony the party infiltrates
2020-04-13 @ 01:40:56.
Shows signs of possession (dark circles, agitation) as he kneels for anointing
2020-04-13 @ 01:48:37.
Transforms into a glabrezu demon mid-ritual, instantly stuns and kills the officiating high priest, and
casts Confusion and Reverse Gravity on the assembled crowd
2020-04-13 @ 01:52:04–02:34:08.
Killed by the party (finishing blow from Kurt Furbank) after a running fight across the
ceiling and floor 2020-04-13 @ 03:35:05.

Unresolved
Whether the real Sir Holton Albright was killed/replaced before the ceremony, or possessed and killed
during it, is never clarified.

npcs/sphinx-painting.title: Sphinx Painting
npcs/sphinx-painting.content:
A sentient, talking painting guarding a secret door in a cult’s abandoned underground complex, demanding
three riddles be answered to pass. Later befriended by the party — especially Miss Cleo — and willing
to leave with them for a new home after centuries alone answering riddles.
History

Animates when Alexander steps on a rug in front of it, demanding three riddles be answered to pass,
lightning-zapping wrong guesses 2021-10-19 @ 00:27:24.
Poses the “letter N” riddle (a king has one, a nun has two, a whore has none), accepted after two failed
guesses 2021-10-19 @ 00:28:10–00:41:50.
Poses the “sawdust” riddle, nearly killing Miss Cleo before Nutty works out the answer
2021-10-19 @ 00:42:03–00:55:19.
Poses the final “time” riddle, answered correctly by Jess
2021-10-19 @ 00:56:20–00:58:02.
Befriended by the party, especially Ozan, and reportedly willing to leave with them for a new home; Ozan
buys a bag of holding to transport the painting
2021-10-19 @ 01:33:16, @ 02:32:22.
Left behind at the one-way portal with Donnie and Ozan rather than carried through
2021-10-19 @ 03:02:21.

npcs/strahd-von-zarovich.title: Strahd von Zarovich
npcs/strahd-von-zarovich.content:
The vampire lord of Castle Ravenloft, who has terrorized Barovia for centuries. Lures outsiders to his
castle under forged invitations, then toys with them through illusions, domination, and mist form rather
than fighting to the death. Murdered his own brother Sergei von Zarovich and the woman Tatiana they
both loved out of jealousy.
History

Sends the party a dinner invitation under his seal, alongside a forged plea letter purportedly from
Kolyan Indirovich — both lead the party to Barovia
2022-12-06 @ 01:07:29, @ 02:15:24.
Greets the party for dinner, playing the organ with his back to them, then vanishes with a maniacal
laugh after being hit with a thrown dinner roll — locking down the castle’s doors, torches, and lights
2022-12-18 @ 00:42:14–00:45:43.
Leaves behind a rope-and-mirror-operated mannequin decoy of himself, later burned by Todd
2022-12-18 @ 00:52:39.
His own journal, the cursed Tome of Strahd, is found hidden under his mattress
2022-12-18 @ 02:09:47.
Carries the party to a prison cell atop his highest spire after a ghost ambush; appears briefly below,
waves, smiles, and turns to mist
2023-01-30 @ 01:10:34, @ 01:33:50.
Revealed via a mind-link from Sergei’s body to have murdered his own brother and Tatiana out of
jealousy 2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.
Fatally drains Donnie’s character near his sealed coffin, turning him into a vampire thrall
2023-01-30 @ 04:56:54–05:19:31.
Found asleep in his coffin — empty but for a teddy bear and blanket when finally forced open; the real
Strahd is not there 2023-02-12 @ 00:43:16.
Ambushes the party in his audience chamber, dominating most of them; forces Todd to attack an ally and
Jess to nearly kill Jake, before escaping as mist after a drawn-out fight
2023-02-12 @ 00:58:14–02:23:45.
Mists away into the walls of his casket room before the golem-trap session begins
2023-03-12 @ 00:19:11.
Revealed to have secretly turned Donovan into his thrall and used him to ambush the party from
within 2023-03-18 @ 00:48:16
onward.

DM notes (spoiler)

The figure seen at the dinner organ may have been Strahd himself baiting the party, or another decoy —
Pat never clarified on-mic whether it was staged like the mannequin found later
2022-12-18 @ 00:42:14, @ 00:52:39.
Donnie’s death and vampirization near Strahd’s coffin was a deliberate trap tied to proximity to the
coffin, not random bad luck — Pat calls it intentional, “the only way he can solve it”
2023-01-30 @ 04:50:29.
Pat confirms OOC the module run is the original 1980s/1984 TSR Ravenloft, not the modern remake
2023-01-30 @ 05:36:35,
2023-03-18 @ 00:33:00.

Unresolved
Strahd is never defeated or even fought to a finish in the recorded sessions — the campaign’s last session
ends with him still alive and the party deep in his castle.

npcs/tatiana.title: Tatiana
npcs/tatiana.content:
A woman both Strahd von Zarovich and his brother Sergei von Zarovich loved. Strahd killed her when
she refused to marry him, along with his own brother.
History

Revealed via a mind-link from Sergei’s body: Strahd murdered Sergei and Tatiana out of jealousy
2023-01-30 @ 04:10:16.
The party realizes, after the fact, that a statue Nutty had smashed earlier in the dungeon depicted her
2023-01-30 @ 04:07:04.

Unresolved
Whether Tatiana’s remains or spirit can still be found anywhere in the castle is raised as a hook but
never followed up on in the recorded sessions.

npcs/the-boot.title: The Boot
npcs/the-boot.content:
Current crime lord of Turgeth’s drug trade, a roughly 12-foot-tall troll who took over after
Riggs fell. Runs a dockside warehouse/shipping operation and is tied to the drug Maka.
History

Established as the new crime lord, replacing Riggs 2025-03-31 @ 00:02:38, @ 00:04:23.
Riggs’s Widow used the Boot’s operation to get herself captured and tracked back to the inspectors’
HQ 2025-03-31 @ 00:19:45.
Flees his burning dockside warehouse by ship as the party raids it
2025-03-31 @ 02:38:24-03:09:40.
Spotted on deck by a hasted, ethereal Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice), unaware he’s being watched, as the
session ends mid-chase 2025-03-31 @ 03:09:40-03:10:13.

Unresolved
Whether the Boot is captured, killed, or escapes is not resolved — the session ends mid-chase. See
Hunt for the Boot.

npcs/the-demon-in-nutty.title: The Demon in Nutty
npcs/the-demon-in-nutty.content:
An invisible, chaotic-evil demon that secretly possessed Nutty’s character
after he touched a cursed soul gem sessions before the possession was revealed — a fact even Nutty’s own
player hadn’t fully known until it came out at the table.
History

Secretly possessing Nutty’s body for an unknown number of prior sessions; revealed when it attacks
Ozan’s character and Tick-Tick
2020-03-24 @ 02:43:50.
Kills Ozan’s character outright with a sneak-attack finishing blow
2020-03-24 @ 01:59:28.
Kills the unconscious Tick-Tick immediately after
2020-03-24 @ 02:22:31.
Describes its own “Possession” ability: if struck down near another creature, that creature must save or
be possessed in turn 2020-03-24 @ 02:58:15.
Banished by the newly-reborn Paladin of Pelor’s holy symbol
2020-03-24 @ 02:42:10.

Unresolved
The demon’s true name/species is never stated beyond the player nickname “Mohawk,” which may just refer
to its token art rather than an in-fiction name.

npcs/the-guard-captain.title: The Guard Captain
npcs/the-guard-captain.content:
“The captain” is Rich and Nutty’s own mid-fight nickname (never used by Jake as DM) for the tough,
twin-bladed fighter who followed Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) downstairs and critically wounded him.
History

Follows Rich’s Monk (DungeonVice) downstairs and critically wounds him for 36 damage
2025-03-31 @ 01:52:32-01:53:30.
Finished off by Nutty’s Arcane Combatant (DungeonVice) (flanked, killed with the Washashaka
shocking-grasp attack); Rich then loots his Boots of Haste from the corpse
2025-03-31 @ 02:47:44-02:48:42.

DM notes (spoiler)
Jake tells the players (OOC) this guard was likely a level 10-11 fighter, info the characters never learn
in-game 2025-03-31 @ 02:55:27-02:57:32.
Unresolved
This page likely does not describe a separate NPC at all. The only named enemy Rich meets in this part of
the warehouse is Fugly (named by Jake @ 01:39:20); Rich runs past him, doubles back to fight him
properly @ 01:41:11, and Jake’s narration still calls him “the orc” mid-fight @ 01:48:40 — right before
this same enemy follows Rich down the stairs @ 01:52:32 and crits him. “The captain” is only ever Rich’s
and Nutty’s own guess at his rank 2025-03-31 @ 01:43:49, @ 01:55:17, never
confirmed by Jake as a second NPC. Treat this page and Fugly as almost certainly the same character
until a future session clarifies otherwise.

npcs/the-mage.title: The Mage
npcs/the-mage.content:
The deceased wizard who built and ran the party’s planeshifting, blood-fueled ship as a deliberate trap
for thieves — draining their blood to power the vessel and fuel his own immortality. Killed by the party
before the recorded sessions begin.
History

Referenced as already dead; the party loots his ship, finds his cosmology journal and hidden spell
book 2020-01-20 @ 00:20:38, @ 00:48:54.
Pat (OOC) reveals his blood-draining trap existed to fund “immortality and interplanar travel powered by
the suffering of someone” 2020-01-20
@ 00:31:05.
His corpse is reanimated by Rich as a “bloody skeleton” undead minion, kept on hand as emergency muscle
2020-03-25 @ 02:19:47.

npcs/the-seated-man.title: The Seated Man
npcs/the-seated-man.content:
An unnamed, cobwebbed figure found motionless on a throne deep in the pyramid, holding a staff and wearing
a skull crown — implied to be the source of the visions that drew the party to the temple.
History

Found seated and statue-still on a throne, implied source of the visions that drew the party to the
temple 2019-10-15 @ 01:49:06.
Awakens hostile, eyes flashing, and joins the fight against the party after Rich fails to steal his
staff (even with a fate-point reroll)
2019-10-15 @ 02:43:22.
Commands a golden/bronze hand guardian built into the boss chamber’s walls
2019-10-15 @ 02:43:22.

Unresolved
The session ends mid-fight against him; his fate, and whether he really is the source of the party’s
visions, is never resolved in the recorded sessions.

npcs/thornshade.title: Thornshade
npcs/thornshade.content:
An investigator for the TIU, a planar law-enforcement organization out of the city of Chrome, hunting
the Dyson Dynamo. Appears only as an astral projection, not physically present.
History

Descends on the party outside the rug shop with his subordinate Iron Soul, identifies the
Dyson Dynamo as a reality-threatening artifact, and demands answers
2023-11-28 @ 00:37:54–00:38:31.
Revealed as an astral projection when Ashleen (leenmcweenersten’s witch) tries to pick his pocket for
a look at his badge and her hand passes right through him @ 00:43:08–00:43:22.
Grabs Ashleen’s hand after she casts Detect Thoughts on him, and warns the party that any further magic
will be treated as an act of aggression @ 00:43:41–00:45:22.
Fought and defeated by Gang in a brawl, his shimmering true form showing through each hit; concedes
@ 01:03:48–01:08:03.
Shows his real badge (TIU, city of Chrome), explains the Dynamo harvests “just and unjust souls,” offers
1,000–2,000 gold compensation, and leaves after the party is marked as suspects @ 01:08:41–01:18:33.

Unresolved
“Chrome” as his home city may be a mistranscription of a different fantasy name.

npcs/volto.title: Volto
npcs/volto.content:
The inspectors’ office/HQ chief.
History

Reminds the team about the still-pending Aqueducts Assignment, grumbling about funding from
“Captain Lieutenant Squats” 2025-03-31 @ 00:07:25-00:07:44.

pcs/aisling.title: Aisling
pcs/aisling.content:
A second character fielded by Donnie alongside Colt Hopper: a small witch with a prehensile tongue,
dual ranged weapons, and hex magic. Her name is transcribed inconsistently as “Ashley,” “Ashleen,”
“Ashlene,” and “Aisling” — “Aisling” is used here as the best-guess spelling.
History

Glimpsed mid-session, 6’1” tall, described as towering over “the little frog dude” (Colt Hopper)
2023-09-12 @ 03:17:53–03:18:01.
Casts Vomit Swarm (wasps) and uses a hex build (Limp Lash, Misfortune, Cackle), targeting the enemy
healer-cleric with Misfortune shortly before the party finishes it off
2023-10-01 @ 00:34:21, @ 02:29:30–02:33:09.
Named among the party’s absent members (player not on the call) in session 4
2023-10-15 @ 00:27:29.
Named among the party’s absent members in session 5
2023-10-24 @ 00:41:43.

Unresolved
A witch named “Ashleen,” played by a different real person (leenmcweenersten, new to the table), appears
in session 6 — using Detect Thoughts and perceiving astral “silver threads.” It’s unclear whether this is
the same character handed to a new player, a coincidence of name, or an unrelated character; the session
6 notes list her separately. See 2023-11-28
@ 00:43:41, @ 01:20:38.

pcs/alexander.title: Alexander
pcs/alexander.content:
Jake’s Arc II character: an android (implied soul knight/psion type) who wields a “dislocator” gun named
Becky and carries a scouting Psycrystal.
History

Triggers a tripwire fire trap, then steps onto the rug that reveals the Sphinx Painting
2021-10-19 @ 00:24:48–00:27:24.
Takes two large lightning hits (30 and 53 damage) failing the Sphinx’s first riddle before Ozan’s
shared memories help him answer correctly
2021-10-19 @ 00:29:11–00:41:50.
Plants his Psycrystal in a dead body’s mouth to remotely scout the Nexus portal’s destination, a frozen
plane with ice golems and a frost giant
2021-10-19 @ 01:08:00–01:14:05.
Finishes forging the sword Ember at the complex’s blacksmith forge
2021-10-19 @ 02:56:23.
Uses his dislocator gun “Becky” to repeatedly teleport the frost giant’s golem escorts dozens of miles
away, removing them from the fight one at a time
2021-11-02 @ 00:20:53–01:16:00.

Unresolved
Whether “Alexander” is his full/official name or just a table nickname is unclear from the transcripts.

pcs/alumbra.title: Alumbra
pcs/alumbra.content:
A ninja/rogue with a katana, sneak attack, uncanny dodge, superior (120 ft.) darkvision, Kai points, and
a Shadow Clone jutsu. Owns a handy haversack, destroyed late in the campaign. In session 1, present
physically at Rich’s location without her own microphone, with Rich’s track picking up and relaying her
dialogue and rolls; from session 2 onward she appears on her own track.
History

Rolls the floating Ion Stone (+2 Constitution) as a starting magic item
2022-12-06 @ 00:52:52.
Finds the secret door behind the dining hall’s organ, leading to the Strahd decoy
2022-12-18 @ 00:51:24.
Gets surrounded and flanked early in the skeleton ambush
2022-12-18 @ 01:08:11.
Trapped in a burning cell during the gas-trap fire; rescued when Donnie’s Air Bubble buys time for
Ozan to pick the lock 2022-12-26
@ 03:30:56–03:53:00.
Turned to stone touching the petrification-warded bars at Strahd’s crypt; restored once the vampire
bride Petrina Velikovna is defeated 2023-01-30
@ 04:13:44–04:20:48.
Under Strahd’s domination, forced to flank and sneak-attack Jake’s character for 21
damage, nearly killing him 2023-02-12 @ 01:20:30–01:27:00.
Takes heavy golem poison damage, rolls a natural 1 fleeing between both iron golems, and uses her Shadow
Clone jutsu to escape, saved by a burned Fate Point
2023-03-12 @ 01:11:50–01:35:24.
Kills the horse-headed demon with a critical sneak attack, and is infected with Contagion by it
2023-03-18.
Her handy haversack — being used to contain Donovan’s vampire-mist form — is destroyed by
Todd, tearing open a gate to the Astral Plane
2023-03-18.

Unresolved
Her name is rendered inconsistently across sessions (Ulumbra, Alhambra, Olumbra, Lulu); “Alumbra” is used
here as the most frequent spelling in later sessions. Whether “Lulu” and “Alumbra” are the same character
is unclear from context around a trap-triggered disappearance
2022-12-26 @ 02:51:59–02:56:12.

pcs/colt-hopper.title: Colt Hopper
pcs/colt-hopper.content:
Donnie’s grippli (frog-folk) gunslinger, 2’2” tall, dual revolvers. Named “Colt Hopper” in session 1 and
“Donovan” in session 6; treated here as one continuous character on the strength of the matching
race/class, with the gap flagged below.
History

Introduced as a 2’2” grippli gunslinger, possibly also multiclassed into witch; buys a Cloak of
Resistance +1 and a Cackling Hag’s Blouse
2023-09-12 @ 02:04:50–02:10:29.
Claims the suitcase of revolver bullets, revolvers, and a gunsmithing tome from the vault chest
2023-10-01 @ 04:23:51–04:24:07.
Absent/played as an NPC fleeing the fight in session 4, shrunk and teleported clear of Godoy by Rich
2023-10-15 @ 00:27:29, @ 01:07:58.
Not present on the call for session 5.
As “Donovan”: demands ID from the TIU investigators; snorts “whimsy” and gains the ability to see
invisible pickpockets; bluffs a goblin racing crew about the party’s carpet; grabs one of the invisible
pickpockets by hand
2023-11-28 @ 00:38:48, @ 02:13:37, @ 02:21:02, @ 02:37:01.

Unresolved
Session 6 is the first to use the name “Donovan” for this character rather than “Colt Hopper”; no session
explicitly confirms they’re the same PC, though the race/class match and no new-character introduction is
narrated.

pcs/dread-pirate-bobbert.title: Dread Pirate Bobbert
pcs/dread-pirate-bobbert.content:
Rich’s Arc I character, an arcane spellcaster (wizard, implied Universalist) who serves as the party’s
utility caster throughout — identifying magic items, flying the party around, and providing most of its
crowd control and escape options. Named “Dread Pirate Bobbert” from
2020-04-13 onward; earlier sessions refer to him only as
“Rich’s character.”
History

Casts Fireball and Hydraulic Torrent to help destroy a splitting clay golem, then is swept away alone
underwater and meets Andrew 2019-10-15
@ 00:51:36, @ 01:13:40.
Identifies the ship’s helm-room crystal as holding a plane shift spell (25 Knowledge: Arcana)
2020-01-20 @ 00:19:19.
Loots 87 gold, a Ring of Protection +1, and a potion from travelers crushed by the ship’s accidental
plane shift 2020-01-20 @ 01:11:29.
Scries the paladin hunting Mori Yoshinari using an enchanted true-seeing crystal ball
2020-01-28 @ 02:19:19–02:29:42.
Is teleported alone into a puzzle room via a circular key and found unconscious, being drained by a
soul-sucking demon; survives after Jake and Donnie intervene
2020-03-25 @ 00:57:32–01:35:19.
Breaks a petrifying basilisk-guardian’s gaze with Wall of Force
2020-03-25 @ 01:33:59.
Casts Disintegrate and summons three fire elementals to free Obadiah Jones from his ice prison
2020-04-06 @ 01:10:17, @ 01:37:47.
Named “Dread Pirate Bobbert” for the first time; mage-hands a damaged journal revealing the god-baby is
“touched by the gods” 2020-04-13 @ 00:32:59.
Hands out potions of fly and featherfall before the party infiltrates the knighting ceremony
2020-04-13 @ 01:28:42.

Unresolved
Whether Bobbert is the same character Rich plays in the 2021 sessions (his own unnamed tank/healer
character) is not stated.

pcs/fish.title: Fish
pcs/fish.content:
Donnie’s Arc II character, a Master Chemist / Vivisectionist Beastmorph alchemist referred to as
“Donovan” in session notes and as “Fish” when Rich plays him in Donnie’s absence.
History

Crafts Cure Serious Wounds extracts and potions for the party; chooses to stay behind at the one-way
portal rather than step through
2021-10-19 @ 02:14:02, @ 03:02:34.
With Donnie absent, piloted by Rich; nearly dropped by the frost giant’s opening ranged freezing ray
2021-11-02 @ 00:10:37–00:11:45.
Lands a flanking sneak bite finishing off one of the giant’s golem escorts
2021-11-02 @ 01:05:21.

Unresolved
Whether “Fish” is a new character or the same “Donovan” alchemist from
2021-10-19 is clear from context (same alchemist build), but
whether this is the same character as Arc I’s Mori Yoshinari is not established — a large time gap
and total change of class/race separate the two. The party discusses at session’s end whether Rich or
someone else should continue playing Fish going forward, or roll a new character.

pcs/frankie.title: Frankie
pcs/frankie.content:
Ozan’s Paladin/Bard, very high Charisma (23), given to preaching “the good word.” Named “Frankie” only
in session 6; unnamed in every earlier session.
History

Preaches at four city guards searching for Mary, rolling a natural 20 to pull their attention, then
holds it with a Fascinate as they all fail their saves, giving the bartender time to slip away
2023-09-12 @ 03:28:42, @ 03:30:06–03:31:46.
Turns invisible on a natural 20 stealth check and hauls the vault’s loot chest toward the exit
2023-10-01 @ 00:48:08–02:09:53.
While invisible, grabs the fallen Dyson Dynamo off the ground and flees with it into an alley;
does not grab Connor’s character, who is left behind to escape the firestorm on his own
2023-10-15 @ 01:18:46–01:19:16.
Disguises in robes and dirt for the refugee column; uses Fascinate to cover Pat’s escape from the
Lutathal gate guards 2023-10-24 @ 00:30:39, @ 01:33:04–01:34:51.
As “Frankie”: attempts diplomacy and casts Detect Evil on the TIU investigators (Connor’s sense-motive
check and Donnie’s read conclude the lead investigator isn’t evil, just on a job); bartered Richard
into servitude to a rug shop rather than pay for a carpet (per the session’s recap)
2023-11-28 @ 00:12:38, @ 00:49:18,
@ 00:53:14, @ 01:11:05–01:11:23.

Unresolved
Named “Frankie” for the first time in session 6; no earlier session gives this character a name.

pcs/gang.title: Gang
pcs/gang.content:
A large monstrous-humanoid half-orca Blood Rager, originally a bar bouncer in Lutathal/Liduriel, recruited
into the party in session 6 — the first session for his player, new to the table.
History

Confronts two astral-projected TIU investigators on his boss’s behalf, biting and clawing Thornshade
until he concedes 2023-11-28 @ 00:57:45–01:08:03.
Recruited into the party outright @ 01:27:09.
Turned away from the racers’ club (the Pierrot) for his size, sneaks in through the basement
@ 02:09:01.
Takes the “whimsy” drug and sprouts an extra row of teeth, permanently upgrading his bite for a week
@ 02:29:00–02:32:38.
Blocks the exit to trap a fleeing pickpocket @ 02:39:20.

Unresolved
His size is stated as “14 feet tall, 1,500 pounds” at one point and “a 17-foot motherfucker” later in the
same session — inconsistent and never reconciled
2023-11-28 @ 01:00:08, @ 02:46:43.

pcs/jace-gandolfini.title: Jace Gandolfini
pcs/jace-gandolfini.content:
A tiefling abjurer, roughly 200+ years old, long-tenured and disreputable professor at Hawthorne College
of Enchantment. Appears only in the interlude session DM’d by Pat; see
2023-10-08 and jakedm Unresolved for
this session’s disconnect from the rest of the campaign.
History

Discovers library evidence a demi-lich may still be alive, and a field report about a map to the Tomb
of Horrors 2023-10-08 @ 00:49:09, @ 00:56:17.
Summons Sarkhan Vol back to Hawthorne via arcane message @ 01:00:30.
Slips his research to Professor Bumblebee during a dull faculty meeting @ 01:15:25.
Fails to dispel or disrupt the cursed map’s illusion @ 01:34:04–01:41:38.
Shares an identical dream with Sarkhan and accepts a Revelation Crystal from a skeleton child, waking
with a brand @ 01:56:37–01:58:19.
Bluffs and barters stockroom clerk Bart into lending crafting materials for bottles of air @ 02:48:26–02:59:42.

Unresolved
No later session returns to Jace, Sarkhan, or the Tomb of Horrors expedition.

pcs/jacques-luceau.title: Jacques Luceau
pcs/jacques-luceau.content:
A Vanara (monkey-folk) monk, fighting with flurry of blows and later elemental (electricity, then fire)
-infused unarmed strikes. His name, Jacques Luceau, is only stated once on mic; he’s addressed by various
nicknames across sessions (Woo-woo, Wu, JB), which may reflect genuine in-fiction nicknames or
transcription drift — see Unresolved.
History

Owns the Shadow Well (a portable-hole-like item) and forces a goblin guide into manacles
2022-12-06 @ 01:17:14, @ 01:31:00.
Throws his dinner roll at Strahd, triggering the castle-wide lockdown that opens
the dungeon crawl 2022-12-18 @ 00:43:04.
